first: चौ॰—हृदय सराहत सीय लोनाई। गुरु समीप गवने दोउ भाई॥
en: Praising Sita's loveliness in their hearts, the two brothers went to the guru. Rama told Kaushika everything, for his nature was simple and untouched by deceit.

first: सुमन पाइ मुनि पूजा कीन्ही। पुनि असीस दुहुँ भाइन्ह दीन्हीँ॥
en: Taking the flowers, the sage did his worship and then blessed the two brothers: 'May your wishes bear fruit.' Hearing this, Rama and Lakshmana were happy.

first: करि भाजन मुनिबर बिज्ञानी। लगे कहन कछु कथा पुरानी॥
en: After eating, the great and wise sage began to tell some old stories. When the day was over, with the guru's leave, the two brothers went to say the evening prayers.

first: प्राची दिसि ससि उयेउ सुहावा। सिय-मुख सरिस देखि सुख पावा॥
en: In the east the lovely moon rose, and seeing it like Sita's face, Rama felt joy. Then he thought again in his mind: the moon is not equal to Sita's face.

first: दो॰—जनम-सिन्धु पुनि बन्धु-बिष, दिन-मलीन सकलङ्क।
en: 'Born in the ocean, with poison for a brother, dim by day and stained with a mark: how can the poor, wretched moon be equal to Sita's face?'

first: चौ॰—घटइ बढ़इ बिरहिनि दुखदाई। ग्रसइ राहु निज सन्धिहि पाई।
en: 'It waxes and wanes, it pains lovers who are apart, and Rahu swallows it when he finds his chance. Moon, you bring grief to the chakva bird and harm to the lotus; you have many faults.'

first: बैदेही-मुख पदतर दीन्हे। होइ दोष बड़ अनुचित कीन्हे॥
en: 'Comparing you to Vaidehi's face would be a great fault and a wrong thing to do.' Praising the beauty of Sita's face under the excuse of the moon, he went back to the guru, seeing that the night was far gone.

first: करि मुनि-चरन-सरोज प्रनामा। आयसु पाइ कीन्ह बिस्त्रामा॥
en: He bowed at the sage's lotus feet and, with his leave, went to rest. When the night was over, the Lord of the Raghus woke and, looking at his brother, began to speak.

first: उयेउ अरुन अवलोकहु ताता। पङ्कज-कोक-लोक सुखदाता॥
en: 'Look, brother, the dawn has risen, which gives joy to the lotus, the chakva bird and the world.' Lakshmana joined his hands and spoke soft words that hinted at the Lord's power.

first: दो॰—अरुनोदय सकुचे कुमुद, उडुगन जोति भलीन।
en: 'At dawn the night lilies close and the light of the stars grows dim; in the same way, on hearing that you have come, the kings have lost their strength.'

first: चौ॰—नृप सब नखत करहिँ उँजियारी। दारिन सकहिँ चाप तम भारी॥
en: 'The kings, like stars, give some light, but they cannot remove the heavy darkness of the bow. Lotuses, chakvas, bees and many birds are all glad when night ends;'

first: ऐसेहि प्रभु सब भगत तुम्हारे। हाेइहहिँ टूटे धनुष सुखारे॥
en: 'just so, Lord, all your devotees will be happy when the bow is broken. The sun has risen and ended the darkness without effort; the stars have hidden and light shines on the world.'

first: रबि निज उदय ब्याज रघुराया। प्रभु प्रताप सब नृपन्ह देखाया॥
en: 'Lord of the Raghus, by the excuse of his rising, the sun has shown all the kings your glory. To reveal the might of your arms, the way to break the bow has come to light.'

first: बन्धु बचन सुनि प्रभु मुसुकाने। होइ सुचि सहज पुनीत नहाने॥
en: Hearing his brother's words, the Lord smiled. Pure by nature, he bathed, did his daily rites, came to the guru and bowed his lovely head at his lotus feet.

first: सतानन्द तब जनक बोलाये। कैासिक मुनि पहिँ तुरत पठाये॥
en: Then Janaka called Shatananda and sent him at once to the sage Kaushika. He came and gave Janaka's humble request, and the sage gladly called the two brothers.

first: दो॰—सतानन्द पद बन्दि प्रभु, बैठे गुरु पहिँ जाइ॥
en: The Lord bowed at Shatananda's feet and went and sat by the guru. Then the sage said, 'Come, dear son, Janaka has sent for us.'

first: चौ॰—सीय-स्वयम्बर देखिय जाई। ईस काहि धौँ देह बड़ाई॥
en: 'Let us go and see Sita's choosing of a husband, and see to whom God gives the honour.' Lakshmana said, 'That one will be worthy of the honour on whom your grace falls, master.'

first: हरषे मुनि सब सुनि बर बानी। दीन्ह असीस सबहि सुख मानी॥
en: All the sages were glad to hear these fine words and blessed him, feeling happy. Then the merciful Lord, with the band of sages, set out to see the hall of the bow sacrifice.

first: रङ्गभूमि आये दोउ भाई। असि सुधि सब पुरबासिन्ह पाई॥
en: Word spread to all the people of the city that the two brothers had come to the arena. Forgetting their housework, all set out, children, young and old, men and women.

first: देखी जनक भीर भइ भारी। सुचि सेवक सब लिये हँकारी ॥
en: When Janaka saw the great crowd, he called all his trusted servants: 'Go at once to all the people and give everyone a fitting seat.'

first: दो॰—कहि मृदु बचन बिनीत तिन्ह, बैठारे नर नारि।
en: With soft, humble words they seated the men and women, high, middle, low and humble, each in a place fitting their rank.

first: चौ॰—राजकुँअर तेहि अवसर आये। मनहुँ मनोहरता तन छाये॥
en: Just then the princes arrived, as if loveliness itself had spread over their bodies. They were oceans of virtue, refined and fine heroes, with lovely bodies, dark and fair.

first: राज-समाज विराजत रुरे। उडुगन महँ जनु जुग विधु पूरे॥
en: They shone in the gathering of kings like two full moons among the stars. Each person saw the Lord's form in keeping with the feeling in their own heart.

first: देखहिँ भूप महा-रन-धीरा। मनहुँ वीररस धरे सरीरा॥
en: The kings, steady in great battles, saw him as if the heroic mood had taken a body. The crooked kings were afraid when they looked at the Lord, as if he were a huge and fearful form.

first: रहे असुर छल छोनिप बेखा। तिन्ह प्रभु प्रगट काल सम देखा॥
en: The demons who were there in the guise of kings saw the Lord clearly as Death. The people of the city saw the two brothers as the ornaments of mankind, a joy to the eyes.

first: दो॰—नारि बिलोकहिँ हरषि हिय, निज निज रुचि अनुरूप।
en: The women looked at him with glad hearts, each according to her own liking, as if love itself had taken a supremely matchless form.

first: चौ॰—बिदुषन्ह प्रभु बिराट मय दीसा। बहु मुख-कर-पग-लोचन-सीसा॥
en: To the learned, the Lord appeared in his cosmic form, with many faces, hands, feet, eyes and heads. Janaka's kin saw him as a dear relative.

first: सहित बिदेह बिलोकहिँ रानी। सिसु सम प्रीति न जाइ बखानी॥
en: The queens, with Videha, looked on him with a love like that for their own child, beyond words. To the yogis he appeared as the supreme reality, calm, pure, even and self-shining.

first: हरिभगतन्ह देखे दोउ भ्राता। इष्टदेव इव सब सुख-दाता॥
en: Hari's devotees saw the two brothers as their chosen deity, the giver of all joy. The feeling with which Sita looked at Rama, that love and joy cannot be told.

first: उर अनुभवति न कहि सक सोऊ। कवन प्रकार कहइ कबि कोऊ॥
en: She felt it in her heart but could not say it; then how can any poet tell it? Each one saw the King of Kosala according to the feeling in their own heart.

first: दो॰—राजत राज-समाज महँ, कोसलराज-किसोर।
en: The princes of Kosala shone in the gathering of kings, with lovely bodies, dark and fair, stealing the eyes of the world.

first: चौ॰—सहज मनेाहर मूरति दोऊ। कोटि-काम उपमा लघु सोऊ॥
en: Both forms were naturally charming, and even millions of Love gods are too small a comparison for them. Their fine faces put the autumn moon to shame, and their lotus eyes won the heart.

first: चितवनि चारु मार-मद-हरनी। भावति हृदय जाति नहिँ बरनी॥
en: Their lovely glances took away the pride of Love; they pleased the heart beyond description. Lovely cheeks with swinging earrings, fine chins and lips, and soft speech.

first: कुमुदबन्धु-कर-निन्दक हासा। भृकुटी बिकट मनोहर नासा॥
en: Their smiles put moonbeams to shame; their brows were curved and their noses lovely. Marks shone on their broad foreheads, and rows of bees felt shy on seeing their hair.

first: पीत चौतनी सिरन्ह सुहाई। कुसुम-कली बिच बीच बनाई॥
en: Yellow square caps looked fine on their heads, with flower buds set here and there. Their lovely conch-like necks had three lines, as if marking the limit of the beauty of the three worlds.

first: दो॰—कुञ्जरमनि-कंठा-कलित, उरन्हि तुलसिका-भाल।
en: They wore necklaces of elephant pearls and garlands of tulsi on their chests. With shoulders like a bull, the stance of a lion and long arms, they were treasures of strength.

first: चौ॰—कटि तूनीर पीत-पट बाँधे। कर-सर धनुष-बाम-बर काँधे॥
en: Quivers were tied at their waists with yellow cloth, arrows were in their hands, and fine bows on their left shoulders. Yellow sacred threads looked lovely on them; from head to toe they were covered in great beauty.

first: देखि लोग सब भये सुखारे। एकटक लोचन चलत न तारे॥
en: Everyone who saw them was happy; their eyes stared without blinking and their pupils did not move. Janaka was glad to see the two brothers and went and clasped the sage's lotus feet.

first: करि बिनती निज कथा सुनाई। रङ्गअवनि सब मुनिहि देखाई॥
en: He humbly told his story and showed the sage the whole arena. Wherever the two fine princes went, everyone gazed at them in wonder.

first: निज निज रुख रामहिँ सब देखा। कोउ न जान कछु चरित बिसेखा॥
en: Each saw Rama facing towards themselves, and no one knew the special secret of it. The sage told the king that the arrangements were fine, and the king was glad and greatly pleased.

first: दो॰—सब मञ्चन्ह तेँ मच्च एक, सुन्दर बिसद बिसाल।
en: Above all the platforms was one platform, lovely, bright and wide; there the king seated the two brothers with the sage.

first: चौ॰—प्रभुहि देखि सब नुप हिय हारे। जनु राकेस उदय भये तारे॥
en: Seeing the Lord, all the kings lost heart, like stars when the full moon rises. Everyone felt sure in their mind that Rama would break the bow without a doubt.

first: बिनु भब्जेहु अव-धनुष विसाला। मेलिहि सीय राम उर माला॥
en: 'Even without breaking the huge bow of Shiva, Sita will put the garland on Rama's neck. Thinking this, brothers, go home, having lost fame, glory, strength and pride.'

first: बिहँसे अपर भूप सुनि बानी। जे अबिबेक अन्ध अभिमानी॥
en: Hearing these words, other kings laughed, those blind with folly and pride: 'Even if he breaks the bow, the marriage is hard to win; without breaking it, who can marry the princess?'

first: एक बार कालहु किन होऊ। सिय हित समर जितब हम सोऊ॥
en: 'Even if Death himself comes once, we will beat him in battle for Sita.' Hearing this, other kings smiled, righteous, wise devotees of Hari.

first: सो॰—सीय बियाहब राम, गरब दूरि करि नृपन्ह को।
en: 'Rama will marry Sita after taking away the pride of the kings. Who can beat Dasharatha's sons in battle, so skilled in war?'

first: ची॰—वृथा मरहु जनि गाल बजाई। मन-मोदकन्हि कि भूख बताई॥
en: 'Do not die in vain by boasting; can sweets in the mind satisfy hunger? Listen to our very pure advice: know in your heart that Sita is the Mother of the world,'

first: जगतपिता रघुपतिहि बिचारी। भरि लोचन छबि लेहु निहारी॥
en: 'and think of the Lord of the Raghus as the Father of the world, and gaze at his beauty with full eyes. Lovely, joy-giving, a store of every virtue, these two brothers live in Shambhu's heart.'

first: सुधा समुद्र समीप बिहाई। मृग-जल निरखि मरहु कत धाई॥
en: 'Why leave the ocean of nectar nearby and run to die chasing a mirage? Go and do whatever you like; we have today gained the reward of our birth.'

first: अस कहि भले भूप अनुरागे। रूप अनूप बिलोकन लागे॥
en: Saying this, the good kings, full of love, began to gaze at the matchless form. The gods in their sky-chariots watched, showering flowers and singing sweetly.

first: दो॰—जानि सुअवसर सीय तब, पठई जनक बोलाइ।
en: Knowing the right moment had come, Janaka sent for Sita. Her clever, lovely and capable friends respectfully brought her.

first: चौ॰—सिय साभा नहिँ जाइ बखानी। जगदम्बिका रूप-गुन-खानी॥
en: Sita's beauty cannot be told; she is the Mother of the world, a mine of beauty and virtue. Every comparison seems small to me, for they are tied to the bodies of ordinary women.

first: सीय बरनि तेहि उपमा देई। कुकबि कहाइ अजस को लेई॥
en: Who would describe Sita with those comparisons and take the shame of being called a bad poet? If one compares Sita with other women, where in the world is a young woman so lovely?

first: गिरा-मुखर तनु-अरध-भवानी। रति अति दुखित अननु पति जानी॥
en: Sarasvati is too talkative, Bhavani has only half a body, and Rati is very sad, knowing her husband has no body. Lakshmi has poison and wine for brothers; how can Vaidehi be called equal to her?

first: जाैँ छवि-सुधा-पयोनिधि होई। परम-रूप-मय कच्छप साई॥
en: If there were an ocean of the nectar of beauty, with supreme beauty as the turtle, splendour as the rope, and grace as Mount Mandara, and if Love himself churned it with his own lotus hands,

first: दो॰—एहि बिधि उपजइ लच्छि जब, सुन्दरता सुख-मूल।
en: and if Lakshmi were born from that, the root of beauty and joy, even then poets would only shyly call her equal to Sita.

first: चौ॰—चली सङ्गलइ सखो सयानी। गावत गीत मनोहर बानी।
en: Her clever friends set out with her, singing songs in charming voices. A lovely sari draped her tender body; the Mother of the world was of matchless, great beauty.

first: भूषन सकल सुदेस सुहाये। अङ्ग अङ्ग रचि सखिन्ह बनाये।
en: All her ornaments, well placed and lovely, had been arranged by her friends on every limb. When Sita stepped into the arena, men and women were charmed by her form.

first: हरषि सुरन्ह दुन्दुभी बजाई। बरषि प्रसून अपछरा गाई॥
en: The gods gladly beat their drums, flowers rained, and the nymphs sang. The victory garland shone in her lotus hands, and all the kings suddenly looked at her.

first: सीय चकित चित रामहि चाहा। भये मोह-बस सब नरनाहा॥
en: Sita, startled, looked for Rama with her mind, while all the kings fell under her spell. She saw the two brothers near the sage, and her eyes eagerly fixed on them, as on a found treasure.

first: दो॰ – गुरुजन लाज समाज बड़, देखि सीय सकुचानि॥
en: Seeing her elders and the great gathering, Sita felt shy, and holding the hero of the Raghus in her heart, she began to look towards her friends.

first: चौ॰ – राम रूप अरु सियछवि देखे। नर नारिन्ह परिहरी निमेखे॥
en: Seeing Rama's form and Sita's beauty, the men and women stopped blinking. All were anxious but too shy to speak, and they prayed to the Creator in their hearts:

first: हरु बिधि बेगि जनक जड़ताई। मति हमारि असि देहि सुहाई॥
en: 'Creator, quickly take away Janaka's stubbornness and give him good sense like ours, so that the king, without a second thought, drops his vow and marries Sita to Rama.'

first: जग मल कहिहि भाव सब काहू। हठ कीन्हे अन्तहु उर दाहू॥
en: 'The world will call it good, and everyone will like it; holding on stubbornly will only burn the heart in the end.' All the people were lost in this longing: the dark bridegroom is right for Janaki.

first: तब बन्दीजन जनक बोलाये। बिरदावली कहत चलि आये॥
en: Then Janaka called his heralds, and they came reciting the family's glories. The king said, 'Go and tell my vow.' The bards went, with no small joy in their hearts.

first: दो॰ – बोले बन्दी बचन बर, सुनहु सकल महिपाल।
en: The heralds spoke fine words: 'Listen, all you kings! Raising our long arms, we tell you the vow of Videha.'

first: चौ॰ – नृप-भुजबल-बिधु सिव-धनु-राहू। गरुअ कठोर बिदित्त सब काहू॥
en: 'The might of kings' arms is the moon, and Shiva's bow is Rahu; it is heavy and hard, as everyone knows. Even the great warriors Ravana and Bana saw the bow and quietly went away.'

first: सोइ पुरारि-कोदंड कठोरा। राज-समाज आजु जेई तोरा॥
en: 'Whoever in this gathering of kings breaks today this hard bow of the enemy of the three cities, Vaidehi will marry him without delay, along with victory over the three worlds.'

first: सुनि पन सकल भूप अभिलाखे। भट मानी अतिसय मन माखे॥
en: Hearing the vow, all the kings were filled with desire, and proud warriors were greatly stirred. Tightening their belts, they rose eagerly and went, bowing to their chosen gods.

first: तमकि ताकि तकि सिव-धनु धरहीँ। उठइ न कोटि भाँति बल करहीँ॥
en: They glared at Shiva's bow, took aim and grabbed it, but though they tried in ten million ways, it would not rise. Those kings who had some sense in their minds did not even go near the bow.

first: दो॰—तमकि धरहिँ धनु मूढ़ नृप, उठइ न चलहिँ लजाइ।
en: Foolish kings grabbed the bow in a rage, but it would not rise, and they went away ashamed, as if the bow, taking in each warrior's strength, grew heavier and heavier.

first: चौ॰—भूप सहस-दस एकहि बारा। लगे उठावन टरइ न टारा॥
en: Then ten thousand kings tried to lift it all at once, but it would not move at all. Shambhu's bow did not stir, just as a faithful wife's mind does not stir at the words of a lustful man.

first: सब नृप भये जोग उपहासी। जैसे बिनु बिराग सन्यासी॥
en: All the kings became a laughing stock, like a monk without detachment. Their fame, victories and great valour were all taken by the bow, and they went away beaten.

first: श्रीहत भये हारि हिय राजा। बैठे निज निज जाइ समाजा॥
en: The kings lost their glow, lost heart, and went and sat among their own people. Seeing the kings, Janaka grew upset and spoke words that seemed soaked in anger.

first: दीप दीप के भूपति नाना। आये सुनि हम जो पन ठाना।
en: 'Hearing the vow I made, kings came from many lands, and many heroes steady in battle came, gods and demons in human bodies.'

first: दो॰—कुँअरि मनोहर बिजय बड़ि, कीरति अति-कमनीय।
en: 'There is a lovely princess, a great victory and very fine fame to be won, but it seems the Creator has not made anyone who can break the bow.'

first: चौ॰—कहहु काहि यह लाभ न भावा। काहुन सङ्कर-चाप चढ़ावा॥
en: 'Tell me, who did not want this prize? Yet no one strung Shankar's bow. Leave aside stringing and breaking it, brothers; no one could move it even a sesame seed's width from the ground.'

first: अब जनि कोउ माखइ भट मानी। बीर-बिहीन मही मैं जानी॥
en: 'Now let no proud warrior take offence; I know the earth is empty of heroes. Give up hope and go home; the Creator has not written Vaidehi's marriage.'

first: सुकृत जाइ जौँ पन परिहरऊँ। कुँअरि कुँआरि रहउ का करऊँ॥
en: 'If I give up my vow, my merit is lost; so let the princess stay unmarried, what can I do? Had I known the earth was empty of heroes, brothers, I would not have made this vow and been laughed at.'

first: जनक बचन सुनि सब नर नारी। देखि जानकिहि भये दुखारी॥
en: Hearing Janaka's words, all the men and women looked at Janaki and grew sad. Lakshmana was angered; his brows bent, his lips quivered and his eyes grew red.

first: दो॰—कहि न सकत रघुबीर डर, लगे बचन जनु बान।
en: In awe of the hero of the Raghus he could not speak, though the words pierced him like arrows. Bowing his head at Rama's lotus feet, he spoke words true to the facts.

first: चौ॰—रघुबंसिन्ह महँ जहँ कोउ होई। तेहि समाज अस कहइ न कोई॥
en: 'Where even one of the Raghu line is present, no one in that gathering speaks like this, as Janaka has spoken such improper words, knowing the jewel of the Raghu clan is here.'

first: सुनहु भानुकुल-पङ्कज भानू। कहउँ सुनाव न कछु अभिमानू॥
en: 'Listen, sun to the lotus of the Sun dynasty, I say this plainly, without pride: if I get your order, I will lift the universe like a ball'

first: काँचे घट जिमि डारउँ फोरी। सकउँ मेरु मूलक इव तोरी॥
en: 'and smash it like a raw clay pot; I can break Mount Meru like a radish. Lord, with the glory of your power, what is this poor old Pinaka bow?'

first: नाथ जानि अस आयसु होई। कौतुक करउँ बिलोकिय सोई॥
en: 'Master, knowing this, give the order and I will put on a show; watch it. I will string the bow like a lotus stalk and run with it a hundred yojanas.'

first: दो॰—तारउँ छत्रकदंड जिमि, तव प्रताप बल नाथ।
en: 'By the strength of your glory, master, I will break it like the stem of a mushroom. If I do not, I swear by the Lord's feet, I will never again take up bow and quiver.'

first: चौ॰—लखन सकोप बचन जब बोले। डगमगानि महि दिग्गज डोले॥
en: When Lakshmana spoke these angry words, the earth shook and the elephants that hold up the quarters swayed. All the people and all the kings were afraid; Sita was glad at heart and Janaka felt ashamed.

first: गुरु रघुपति सन्न मुनि मन माहीँ। मुदित भये पुनि पुनि पुलकाहीँ॥
en: The guru, the Lord of the Raghus and all the sages were pleased at heart and thrilled again and again. With a sign the Lord of the Raghus stopped Lakshmana and lovingly seated him near himself.

first: बिस्वामित्र समय सुभ जानी। बोले अति-सनेह-मय बानी॥
en: Knowing the time was right, Vishvamitra spoke with great affection: 'Rise, Rama, break Shiva's bow, and, dear son, take away Janaka's distress.'

first: सुनि गुरु बचन चरन सिर नावा। हरष विषाद न कछु उर आवा॥
en: Hearing the guru's words, he bowed his head at his feet, with neither joy nor sorrow in his heart. He stood up in his natural way, with a stance that would shame a young lion.

first: दो॰—उदित उदय-गिरि मञ्च पर, रघुबर बाल-पतङ्ग।
en: As Rama, like the young sun, rose on the platform as on the eastern mountain, all the saints opened like lotuses and the bees of their eyes rejoiced.

first: चौ॰—नृपन्ह केरिआसानिसि नासी। बचन नखत अवलीन प्रकासी॥
en: The night of the kings' hopes ended, and the light of their boasting stars faded. The proud kings closed up like night lilies, and the false kings hid like owls.

first: भये बिसोक कोक मुनि देवा। बरषहिँ सुमन जनावहिँ सेवा॥
en: The sages and gods were freed from grief like chakva birds, and showered flowers to offer their service. Bowing lovingly at the guru's feet, Rama asked the sages for leave.

first: सहजहि चले सकल जग स्वामी। मत्त मञ्जु बर कुञ्जर-गामी॥
en: The lord of the whole world moved in his natural way, with the graceful gait of a fine, proud elephant. As Rama moved, all the men and women of the city were filled with joy, their bodies thrilling.

first: बन्दि पितर सुर सुकृत सँभारे। जौँ कछु पुन्य प्रमाउ हमारे॥
en: Bowing to their ancestors and gods, they remembered their good deeds: 'If any of our merit has power, then, Lord Ganesha, may Rama break Shiva's bow like a lotus stalk.'

first: दो॰—रामहिँ प्रेम समेत लखि, सखिन्ह समीप बोलाइ।
en: Looking at Rama with love, Sita's mother, moved by affection, called her friends near and spoke sadly.

first: चौ॰—सखि सब कौतुक देखनिहारे। जेउ कहावत हितू हमारे॥
en: 'Friends, all these people are just watching the show, even those who call themselves our well-wishers. No one advises the king, saying, "These are boys; such stubbornness is not good."'

first: रावन बान छुआ नहिँ चापा। हारे सकल भूप करि दापा॥
en: 'Ravana and Bana did not even touch the bow, and all the kings were beaten in spite of their pride. Yet they give that bow into the hands of a young prince; can a young swan lift Mount Mandara?'

first: भूप सयानप सकल सिरानी। सखि बिधिगति कछु जाति न जानी॥
en: 'All the king's good sense is gone; friend, the ways of fate cannot be known.' A clever friend spoke gently: 'Queen, one who has great power should not be thought small.'

first: कहँ कुम्भज कहूँ सिन्धु अपारा। सोखेउ सुजस सकल संसारा।
en: 'Think of the pot-born sage Agastya and the endless ocean, which he drank up, and his fame spread over the whole world. The sun's disc looks small, but when it rises the darkness of the three worlds flees.'

first: दो॰—मन्त्र परम-लघु जासु बस, बिधि हरि हर सुर सर्ब।
en: 'A very short mantra holds Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and all the gods in its power. A huge, maddened elephant is controlled by a small goad.'

first: चौ॰—काम कुसुम-धनु-सायक लीन्हे। सकल भुवन अपने बस कीन्हे॥
en: 'Love, with his bow and arrows of flowers, has brought all the worlds under his power. Lady, knowing this, give up your doubt; listen, Rama will surely break the bow.'

first: सखी बचन सुनि भइ परतीती । मिटा बिषाद बढ़ी अति प्रीती॥
en: Hearing her friend's words, the queen felt trust; her sorrow went and her love grew greatly. Then Vaidehi, looking at Rama, anxiously prayed in her heart to one god after another.

first: मनहीं मन मनाव अकुलानी। होहु प्रसन्न महेस भवानी॥
en: Troubled, she prayed silently in her heart, 'Mahesh and Bhavani, be pleased with me. Make my service to you bear fruit; be kind to me and take away the bow's weight.'

first: गन-नायक बर-दायक देवा। आजु लगे कीन्हिउँ तव सेवा॥
en: 'Lord of the Ganas, god who gives boons, I have served you to this day. Hear my prayer again and again, and make the bow's weight very small.'

first: दो॰—देखि देखि रघुबीर छबि, सुर मानव धरि धीर॥
en: Gazing again and again at the beauty of the hero of the Raghus, she prayed to the gods and took courage, her eyes filled with tears of love and her body thrilling.

first: चौ॰—नीके निरखि नयनभरि सोभा। पितु-पनसुमिरि बहुरि मन छोभा।
en: Gazing well at his beauty with full eyes, she remembered her father's vow and her mind was troubled again: 'Alas, father has set his heart on a cruel stubbornness and sees neither gain nor loss.'

first: सचिव समय सिख देइ न कोई। बुध-समाज बड़ अनुचित होई॥
en: 'No minister gives him timely advice; in an assembly of the wise this is a great wrong. Where is the bow harder than a thunderbolt, and where this dark, soft-bodied young prince?'

first: बिधि केहि भाँति धरउँ उर धीरा। सिरस सुमन कन बेधिय हीरा॥
en: 'O Creator, how can I keep courage in my heart? Can a diamond be pierced by a sirisa flower's tip? The whole assembly's sense has gone astray; now, bow of Shambhu, you are my only hope.'

first: निज जड़ता लोगन्ह पर डारी। होहि हरुअर रघुपतिहि निहारी॥
en: 'Throw your hardness onto the people and become light on seeing the Lord of the Raghus.' Sita's mind was in great torment, and each moment passed like a hundred ages.

first: दो॰—प्रभुहि चितइ पुनि चितव महि, राजत लोचन लाल।
en: She looked at the Lord and then at the ground, and her restless eyes shone, as if two fish of Love were playing in the moon's disc.

first: चौ॰—गिरा-अलिनि मुख पङ्कज रोकी। प्रगट न लाज-निसा अवलोकी।
en: The bee of speech was held in the lotus of her mouth, and did not come out, seeing the night of shyness. Tears stayed in the corners of her eyes, like gold in the hands of a great miser.

first: 'सकुची ब्याकुलता बड़िजानी। धरि धीरज प्रतीति उर आनी॥
en: She felt shy, seeing how great her distress was, then took courage and brought faith into her heart: 'If in body, mind and speech my vow is true, and my heart is set on the lotus feet of the Lord of the Raghus,'

first: तौ भगवान सकल उर बासी। करिहहिँ माहिँ रघुपति के दासी॥
en: 'then God, who lives in every heart, will make me the servant of the Lord of the Raghus. Whoever has true love for someone surely finds that one; there is no doubt.'

first: प्रभु तन चितइ प्रेम पन ठाना। कृपानिधान राम सब जाना॥
en: Looking at the Lord, she made a vow of love. Rama, the treasure of mercy, knew it all. Glancing at Sita, he looked at the bow as Garuda looks at a little snake.

first: दो॰—लखन लखेउ रघुबंस-मनि, ताकेउ हर-कोदंड
en: Lakshmana saw that the jewel of the Raghu line had looked at Shiva's bow; his body thrilled and, pressing the universe under his feet, he spoke.

first: चौ॰—दिसि कुञ्जरहु कमठ अहि कोला। धरहु धरनि धरि धीर न डोला॥
en: 'Elephants of the quarters, Tortoise, Serpent and Boar, hold the earth steady and do not let it shake. Rama wants to break Shankar's bow; hear my order and be ready.'

first: चाप समीप राम जब आये। नर नारिन्ह सुर सुकृत मनाये॥
en: When Rama came near the bow, men and women prayed to the gods and their merits. The doubt and ignorance of everyone, the pride of the foolish kings,

first: भृगुपति केरि गरब गरुआई। सुर-मुनिबरन्ह केरि कदराई॥
en: the heavy pride of Parashurama, the fear of the gods and great sages, Sita's worry, Janaka's regret and the burning grief of the queens,

first: सम्भु-चाप बड़ बोहित पाई। चढ़े जाइ सब सङ्ग बनाई॥
en: all these together found Shambhu's bow to be a great ship and boarded it. They wanted to cross the endless ocean of Rama's strength of arm, but there was no helmsman.

first: दो॰—राम बिलोके लोग सब, चित्र लिखे से देखि।
en: Rama looked at all the people and saw them standing still like painted pictures. Then the home of mercy looked at Sita and knew she was in great distress.

first: चौ॰—देखी बिपुल बिकल बैदेही। निमिष बिहोत कलप सम तेही॥
en: He saw Vaidehi was very distressed, and each moment passed for her like an age. If a thirsty person dies for lack of water, what use is a lake of nectar once he is dead?

first: का बरषा जब कृषी सुखाने। समय चुके पुनि का पछिताने॥
en: What use is rain when the crop has dried? What use is regret once the moment has passed? Thinking this, he looked at Janaki, and seeing her deep love, the Lord thrilled.

first: गुरुहि प्रनाम मनहिँ मन कीन्हा। अतिलाघव उठाइ धनु लीन्हा॥
en: He bowed to the guru in his heart and lifted the bow with great ease. As he took it, it flashed like lightning, and then the bow became like a circle in the sky.

first: लेत चढ़ावत खैँचत गाढ़े। काहु न लखा देख सच ठाढ़े॥
en: No one saw him take it, string it or draw it hard; they only saw him standing. In that instant Rama broke the bow in the middle, and a terrible, harsh sound filled the worlds.

first: भरे भुवन घोर कठोर रव रबि, बाजि तजि मारग चले।
en: The terrible, harsh sound filled the worlds; the sun's horses left their path; the elephants of the quarters trumpeted; the earth shook; the Serpent, Boar and Tortoise squirmed. Gods, demons and sages put their hands over their ears and all wondered in alarm; then, says Tulsi, knowing that Rama had broken the bow, they cried out, 'Victory!'

first: सो॰—सङ्कर-चाप 'जहाज, सागर रघुबर बाहुबल॥
en: Shankar's bow was the ship and the strength of Rama's arm the ocean; the whole crowd that had boarded it in delusion was drowned.
